en: The takeover itself is correct, the stale-executable guard doing its job; what was unowned was the aftermath. The superseded process kept its socket, its peer board and its generation of the layer, and answered GET / with the same name and repository_id as the leaseholder, so every liveness test in the system passed on it. Measured on 2026-09-10 - two servers of one checkout, one lease, and a session whose environment carried the older address reading a board with one peer where the shared board had two. GET / now carries leaseholder (lease::LEASEHOLDER_KEY, read by lease::probe, so writer and reader cannot drift), a new initialize is refused <n1/> lease_lost naming the launcher, and health.report's server check warns that this process is not the server it describes. A server too old to answer the question is accepted by the probe on purpose - refusing it would take over a live server, which is how one checkout comes to have two. The doctrine is project.shared-server-resilience.

Změřeno 2026-09-10 - dva servery jednoho checkoutu, jeden lease a relace, jejíž prostředí nesla starší adresu a četla nástěnku s jedním peerem, zatímco sdílená nástěnka měla dva. GET / nyní nese leaseholder (lease::LEASEHOLDER_KEY, čte ho lease::probe, takže zapisovatel a čtenář se nemohou rozejít), nový initialize je odmítnut s <n1/> lease_lost a jménem launcheru a kontrola serveru v health.report varuje, že tento proces není serverem, který popisuje.
